text: dsh-nonead-universal-robots 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的 Universal Robots 机械臂控制插件。它通过 DSH 工具接口连接常见 UR 机器人，并由常驻 Python worker 管理按 IP 建立的连接。用户可以查询机器人状态、TCP 位姿和关节角，也可发送运动、程序与设备控制指令；右侧栏还提供只读 3D 数字孪生，用于查看机器人状态。适合需要在 DSH 会话中读取或控制 UR 机械臂的场景。运行需要 Python 解释器以及可连接的机器人；运动与程序指令默认要求人工确认。

dsh-nonead-universal-robots connects UR arms to DSH with native tools and a Python worker. It reads robot status and poses, issues motion and program commands, and shows a read-only 3D twin in the web sidebar. Python and a reachable robot are required; motion commands need approval by default.

**A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that lets you control Universal Robots (UR) collaborative arms directly from natural language, developed by Suzhou Nonead Robot Technology Co., Ltd. based on the same logic as the company's own nUR MCP Server.** ([Suzhou Nonead Robot Technology Co., Ltd.](https://www.nonead.com))

dsh-nonead-universal-robots README · dsh-nonead-universal-robots：The plugin starts a persistent Python worker (which internally reuses the vendored `URBasic` library) and exposes robot control as **native DSH tools**: the tools talk to the robot through that worker, so after a single `connect` you can keep issuing commands to the same IP. Repository: <https://github.com/NoneadChina/dsh-nonead-universal-robots>

dsh-nonead-universal-robots README · dsh-nonead-universal-robots：> ⚠️ **Safety notice**: this plugin drives a real robotic arm directly. Always keep the robot in sight, keep the emergency stop within reach, and keep the workspace clear of people and obstacles. Treat it with the same care as granting a model the `bash` tool. You (or the model) bear full responsibility for any motion command.

dsh-nonead-universal-robots README · dsh-nonead-universal-robots：> 🧭 **Pre-flight safety gate**: a second layer that caps what a *single* command may ask for, independent of the approval gate. Limits: `safetyMaxStepM` (0.5 m — axis moves **and** drawing dimensions), `safetyMaxLinearSpeed` (0.5 m/s), `safetyMaxJointSpeed` (1.05 rad/s), `safetyMaxAccel` (2.0 m/s²), `safetyMaxDurationS` (60 s), `safetyMaxForceN` / `safetyMaxTorqueNm` (40 N / 10 N·m, force mode), plus an optional `safetyWorkspace` box (`"x:-1,1 y:-1,1 z:0,1.2"`) checked against explicit Cartesian targets — including the `center`/`origin` of the four `ur_draw_*` tools (and their `r` / `border` / `width` / `height` / `side` are capped by `safetyMaxStepM`). It runs **before** the approval prompt — an impossible request should not bother a human — and is **decoupled** from it: `requireApprovalForMotion: false` turns off the human confirmation only, never these physical caps; that requires `safetyGate: false`. A malformed `safetyWorkspace` **fails closed** (every motion op is refused) instead of being silently ignored. It is a guard against typos and unit mistakes, **not** a safety boundary (the controller's own safety conf

dsh-nonead-universal-robots README · Feature overview：Every tool except `connect` takes an `ip` argument and requires that IP to be **connected first**.

---

dsh-nonead-universal-robots README · Read-only 3D digital twin：The plugin also ships a **read-only 3D digital twin** of the robot, rendered with three.js: the entry is a card in the **right sidebar's Start panel**, directly below the "Workspace files / New terminal / Browser" cards, and selecting it fills the right sidebar's content area with the live 3D view. The view subscribes to the host's **SSE stream** (`/twin/stream`, one frame every 100 ms) and stays in sync with the live robot's **joint poses, tool (TCP) coordinate frame and recent motion trajectory**. The twin is **strictly read-only — it never sends a command to the robot**: it only subscribes to the host's read-only routes and renders what it receives. A toolbar offers a reset-view control plus isometric / front / side / top presets, and the camera and base grid are framed from the model's bounding box, so a UR3 and a UR20 are both framed correctly. The numeric panel also shows the dashboard-side state (safety mode, robot mode, program state, speed scaling, joint temperatures, bus voltage/current), taken from the same route on a slower cadence.

dsh-nonead-universal-robots README · Read-only 3D digital twin：The feed does not stall while the robot moves: telemetry is **pushed by the worker** at 20 Hz, and every twin frame reads that push cache first — **without touching the single-threaded command queue**, which is what a running motion confirmation loop occupies. On the wire a push is simply a JSON line without `id`, so an older host treats it as an unmatched response and nothing breaks. Only when the cache is stale (>300 ms) or missing does the twin fall back to an explicit read, and twin reads still use a dedicated **2.5 s budget with `killOnTimeout:false`** — a read-only visualisation read must never destroy the robot session (RTDE/Dashboard) just because it was busy. If a stall does happen, the stream emits `stale` events and the panel says "data stopped updating Ns · retrying" rather than leaving a silently frozen arm on screen. After a disconnect the stream reconnects indefinitely (exponential backoff capped at 30 s) and retries immediately when the window becomes visible again or the feed has been stalled too long. Set `DSH_UR_TWIN_PUSH=0` to turn the push channel off for comparison.

dsh-nonead-universal-robots README · Read-only 3D digital twin：It follows the desktop app's colour theme: the panel's DOM half is coloured with the host's design tokens (`--dsw-alias-*`), so the toolbar, HUD and status line flip automatically with whatever theme is selected under Settings → Appearance (and with third-party themes) — **no JS needed**. The base grid lines and the fallback arm's material colour inside the WebGL canvas are repainted on a theme change by `src/client/theme.js`, which watches `body[data-ds-dark-theme]` (CSS cannot reach values inside WebGL). Theme detection only trusts that attribute and never falls back to the system preference.

dsh-nonead-universal-robots README · Read-only 3D digital twin：| Route | Description |
|---|---|
| `GET /dsh-nonead-ur/twin/stream[?ip=<ip>]` | **SSE stream** (what the client uses by default): one full state frame every 100 ms, plus `stale` (this frame's read has not returned yet) and `frame-error` (this frame failed) events |
| `GET /dsh-nonead-ur/twin/state[?ip=<ip>][&detail=1]` | Live pose (joint angles / TCP / model). `detail=1` adds the dashboard-side state (safety mode, run state, speed scaling, joint temperatures/currents); the pose channel keeps polling independently and a failing detail query never takes it down |
| `GET /dsh-nonead-ur/twin/asset?model=<urXX>` | GLB mesh, with a content-hash `ETag` + `immutable` and `If-None-Match` → 304 support |
| `GET /dsh-nonead-ur/twin/models` | The model list actually present locally |

dsh-nonead-universal-robots README · Read-only 3D digital twin：Failure responses carry a **machine-readable `code`** (`no_robot` / `robot_not_connected` / `ambiguous_robot` / `worker_unavailable` / `robot_error`) and echo the resolved `ip`, so the UI can say which of four very different failures happened. A read that is only **temporarily** unavailable (most often because the worker is busy executing a motion command) is not reported as `robot_error`: the host replays the last known reading with `stale:true` (for up to 30 s), so the twin keeps its picture and says the data is stale. A replayed frame never carries approval state — `pending_motion` is re-read live, so a finished approval cannot keep being drawn as a ghost target.

dsh-nonead-universal-robots README · Languages (UI copy)：Since **0.8.0** the twin panel and the right-dock entry are localised into **eight languages**:

> 简体中文 · English · 日本語 · Español · Français · Deutsch · Русский · Português (Brasil)

dsh-nonead-universal-robots README · Languages (UI copy)：The language **follows the DSH Desktop app language**: the eight dictionaries are registered with the
host's `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-locale` (`dsh.client.inject` + `ctx.locale.register('ur-twin', …)`),
and the host's `locale.preference` decides which one is used. Switching the language in
**Settings → 界面语言 / Language** updates the panel **without a reload**. Without a host locale
service the plugin falls back to `navigator.languages` → `navigator.language` → Simplified Chinese.

dsh-nonead-universal-robots README · Languages (UI copy)：Every user-visible string lives in one table ([`src/client/strings.js`](./src/client/strings.js)), so
adding a language means adding one dictionary — the key set is enforced by tests.

dsh-nonead-universal-robots README · Python runtime：The plugin needs a usable Python with `numpy` and `paramiko` to start the worker:

```sh
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

dsh-nonead-universal-robots README · Python runtime：> ⚠️ **Install those dependencies for the interpreter the worker actually uses.** `lib/worker.js`
> points `PYTHONPATH` at the plugin's `python/` directory, and CPython imports `sitecustomize.py`
> from there at startup if it exists — so a machine-local `sitecustomize.py` that pokes a user-level
> `site-packages` into `sys.path` "works" on one machine and fails everywhere else. Point `pythonBin`
> at an interpreter (or a venv) that has the dependencies.

dsh-nonead-universal-robots README · Python runtime：`pythonBin` (default `python`), `commandTimeoutMs` (motion/script timeout, default `60000`) and `connectTimeoutMs` (first-connect timeout, default `30000`) are configurable in `cordis.patch.yml`. If `python` is not on PATH, use an absolute path, e.g. `"C:\\Python312\\python.exe"` or `"/usr/bin/python3"`. `ur_ping` / `npm run test:python` is the self-check for this chain.

dsh-nonead-universal-robots README · Health check / testing：Verify the plugin and Python runtime without touching a real robot:

```sh
npm run test:python   # python ur_worker.py --selfcheck: verify Python/numpy/paramiko/URBasic/RTDE config
npm test              # 56 items: all 42 test files + 9 gates + 5 offline probes, then a summary
npm run test:node     # Node side only: skip the test files *and* the gates that need Python
npm run check         # all static + cross-language gates without running the test files

dsh-nonead-universal-robots README · Health check / testing：- **42 test files** under `test/` (end-to-end protocol self-check, approval gate, twin routes, client state machine, FK, vendored-library regressions) — enumerated from `test/test-manifest.json`, which `check:manifest` keeps honest so a Python-using file can never be silently unlisted.
- **9 check gates** plus **5 offline probes**: `check-test-manifest` / `check-package-metadata` / `check-client-bundle` / `check-doc-tools` (Node) and `check-worker-ops` / `check-tool-params` / `check-rtde-recipe` / `check-approval-gate` / `check-new-ops` (Python), then the `scripts/probe-*.mjs` twin/SSE probes.
- The **host compatibility check** is also attempted (`check-host-compat --allow-missing-host`). It is an *environment* check, so it is reported on its own summary line and **excluded from the 56-item count**: a machine without DSH Desktop gets a loud `SKIP` with the reason, never a silent pass; a machine (or CI) that provides a host turns it into `PASS — 宿主真实 value-schema DSL 校验通过`.

dsh-nonead-universal-robots README · Health check / testing：**Skipped is not green.** A run with any skipped item exits non-zero — the only way to accept skips is to ask for them explicitly (`--allow-skip`, or `--skip-python` for the Node-only run), and a run in which *everything* was skipped always fails. Two probes need a global `EventSource` and run with `--experimental-eventsource` (Node ≥22.3); between that and `module.registerHooks` (Node ≥22.15) the real development floor is recorded in `devEngines`.

dsh-nonead-universal-robots README · Health check / testing：`npm test` prints a per-item summary. If `python` is not on PATH, set it via the environment:

```sh
UR_PYTHON=C:\\Python312\\python.exe npm test
```

Run the **host compatibility check** before a release and whenever the DSH runtime is upgraded — it validates the plugin against an installed host instead of a copy of its keyword list:

dsh-nonead-universal-robots README · Health check / testing：```sh
npm run verify:host                                # strict: exits 2 when no installed host is found
npm run check:host                                 # same check, but a missing host is a loud SKIP
node scripts/check-host-compat.mjs <node_modules>  # or an explicit host
node scripts/check-host-compat.mjs --host-asar "<...>/resources/app.asar"  # DSH Desktop installs

dsh-nonead-universal-robots README · Health check / testing：It checks the peer ranges against the installed versions, compiles **every** tool parameter schema with the host's real value-schema DSL (a rejected schema silently drops that tool), drives the host route registration, and validates the `dsh.client` declaration plus the client bundle's `__ModuleLoader__` id. Exit code `0` means this plugin works with that host, and it reports how many tools registered out of how many were declared (currently `104/104`).

dsh-nonead-universal-robots README · Health check / testing：`--host-asar` reads the Electron `app.asar` directly (DSH Desktop's normal install shape, where `node_modules` is packed inside the archive): the needed packages are extracted lazily to a temp directory and the real host DSL still runs. `prepublishOnly` is `npm run check && npm run check:host:strict && npm test`, so a release can no longer be made without a real host check or without the test suite.

dsh-nonead-universal-robots README · Health check / testing：When `--host-asar` is omitted, the script auto-discovers a DSH Desktop install (`Program Files`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs`, and `<drive>:\Software\<vendor>` are scanned; candidates whose directory name contains `dsh` win, so an unrelated Electron app that happens to bundle `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` is not picked first). Set `DSH_HOST_ASAR=<...>/resources/app.asar` to pin an archive explicitly.

dsh-nonead-universal-robots README · Health check / testing：CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs the same two commands on Node 22.15/24 × Python 3.9/3.12 with a full checkout (the 14 GLB assets are regular git objects and are really read by the model tests).

> The first `ur_connect` to a robot has an ~20 s RTDE readiness wait; on timeout it returns a clear error rather than hanging.

dsh-nonead-universal-robots README · Host compatibility：The compatibility boundary lives in `package.json` → `peerDependencies`, and `npm run check:host:strict` validates it against the **host's real schema DSL** — not just version numbers: it actually registers all 104 tools into the host, drives the twin routes and checks the `dsh.client` declaration.

dsh-nonead-universal-robots README · Host compatibility：- **Stable releases**: `>=0.1.2-rc.1 <0.3.0` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh` / `dsh-tools`), `>=4.0.2 <5.0.0` (`cordis`), `>=3.18.2 <4.0.0` (`schemastery`) — any stable release in those ranges is covered without touching the declaration.
- **Pre-releases**: semver only matches a pre-release when the range explicitly names that same `major.minor.patch`. Each pre-release triple therefore needs its own clause (e.g. `>=0.2.2-alpha.2 <0.2.3`). When the host publishes a pre-release with a new patch number (say `0.2.3-alpha.1`), `check:host:strict` fails **and prints the exact clause to append**.
- **Historical matrix**: `scripts/check-host-compat.mjs` pins a set of historical/current host versions and re-checks on every run that the declaration still covers them — narrowing the range turns this red immediately, so adopting a new host can't silently drop an old one.
- **Old config and old data**: every cordis config field has a default, so a profile left with an older config (even just `pythonBin`) still parses and takes the defaults; pose files carry their own `version`, the audit ledger is an append-only NDJSON, and program files are plain `.u

dsh-nonead-universal-robots README · How it works：```
DSH model        @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools        python/ur_worker.py          UR robot
  │  ur_movej(...)  │                              │                          │
  ├────────────────►  ctx.tools.register(defineTool)                        │
  │                  │  lib/worker.js               │                          │

dsh-nonead-universal-robots README · How it works：- **`python/ur_worker.py`** — a persistent stdio JSON worker. It keeps `ROBOTS` / `ROBOT_MODELS` dicts, connects by IP, and runs one command per call. Motion commands use (bounded) "arrival confirmation" polling and return a structured error on failure.
- **`lib/worker.js`** — lazily starts the worker once and keeps it alive, matching line-delimited JSON requests/responses, with timeout and cancel (forwards `exec.signal`).
- **`lib/index.js`** — the Cordis plugin that imports `defineTool` to register the above as tools; `inject: ['tools']`.

dsh-nonead-universal-robots README · Tool naming & examples：Tool names are stable as `ur_*`. Example prompts:

> Connect to 192.168.1.199 and read the current TCP pose.

```
ur_connect(ip="192.168.1.199")
ur_get_tcp_pose(ip="192.168.1.199")
```

> Lower the TCP of 192.168.1.199 by 20 mm along the Z axis.

```
ur_get_tcp_pose(ip="192.168.1.199")
ur_move_z(ip="192.168.1.199", distance=-0.02)
```

> Draw a circle of radius 50 mm (vertical plane).

```
ur_draw_circle(ip="192.168.1.199", center=[0.3,-0.2,0.4,0,3.14,0], r=0.05)
```

dsh-nonead-universal-robots README · Notes / limitations：- **Connection persistence** — the worker process lives for the plugin's lifetime and keeps robot connections by IP; after a worker crash or a DSH restart you must `connect` again.
- **Remote control mode** — some UR robots must be in "remote control" before they execute motion/program commands, and `ur_connect` reports that state. **CB3 robots running URSoftware 3.1 through 3.20 already allow remote control by default**; a `remote_control: false` reading still means the controller is *currently* not in remote mode — in local/teach-pendant mode URScript and motion commands are silently discarded, so switch the pendant to remote control. Other firmware (e-Series, or CB3 outside that range) needs Remote Control enabled in PolyScope first. An unreadable state is reported as unknown rather than pretended to be `false`.
- **Reads you cannot trust are reported as such** — a state-setting command that has no read-back channel answers `verified: false`; a controller that refuses the RTDE session is reported as not running instead of "connected"; a twin frame that could not be refreshed is flagged `stale`.
